findings.title: God module: portfolio.service.ts exceeds 2200 LOC with mixed responsibilities
findings.description: The portfolio service in apps/api/src/app/portfolio/portfolio.service.ts contains 2220 lines of code handling multiple distinct responsibilities: portfolio calculations, data aggregation, holdings management, and performance analytics. This violates single responsibility principle and makes the module difficult to test, maintain, and extend.

locations.snippet: Service handles portfolio calculations, data aggregation, holdings management, performance analytics, and more

findings.suggested_fix: Split into domain-specific services: PortfolioCalculationService, PortfolioHoldingsService, PortfolioPerformanceService, PortfolioAggregationService

findings.title: God module: admin.service.ts exceeds 900 LOC with disparate concerns
findings.description: The admin service (apps/api/src/app/admin/admin.service.ts) contains 938 lines handling user management, data cleanup, market data operations, import processing, and analytics. This mixes administrative, data management, and processing logic.

locations.snippet: Service handles user admin operations, data cleanup, market data management, imports, and analytics

findings.suggested_fix: Split into AdminUserService, AdminDataCleanupService, AdminMarketDataService, AdminAnalyticsService

findings.title: God module: data-provider.service.ts exceeds 800 LOC with multiple provider implementations
findings.description: The data-provider service (apps/api/src/services/data-provider/data-provider.service.ts) contains 866 lines and manages the orchestration logic for multiple external data providers (AlphaVantage, Yahoo Finance, CoinGecko, etc.). It acts as a facade but lacks proper abstraction.

locations.snippet: Orchestrates multiple data provider implementations with complex routing logic

findings.suggested_fix: Create a DataProviderRegistry/Factory pattern and move provider-specific logic to individual provider services

findings.title: God module: user.service.ts exceeds 700 LOC with mixed user concerns
findings.description: The user service (apps/api/src/app/user/user.service.ts) contains 733 lines handling user profile management, settings, preferences, and related operations. Should be split by domain responsibility.

locations.snippet: Handles user profile, settings, preferences, and various user-related operations

findings.title: God module: helper.ts in libs/common contains 476 LOC of unrelated utility functions
findings.description: The helper.ts file (libs/common/src/lib/helper.ts) contains 476 lines of general-purpose utility functions covering date manipulation, formatting, validation, and data transformation. This creates a dumping ground for utilities.

locations.snippet: Contains unrelated utility functions for dates, formatting, validation, and transformations

findings.suggested_fix: Split into: date-helper.ts, format-helper.ts, validation-helper.ts, data-transform-helper.ts

findings.title: God module: personal-finance-tools.ts exceeds 1100 LOC with complex calculations
findings.description: The personal-finance-tools.ts (libs/common/src/lib/personal-finance-tools.ts) contains 1145 lines with multiple financial calculation algorithms (FIRE, retirement, tax-loss harvesting). These calculations should be in separate, testable modules.

locations.snippet: Multiple complex financial calculation algorithms mixed in single file

findings.suggested_fix: Split into FireCalculator, RetirementCalculator, TaxLossHarvestingCalculator, etc.

findings.title: Missing service layer abstraction in portfolio calculations
findings.description: The portfolio calculator (apps/api/src/app/portfolio/calculator/portfolio-calculator.ts) contains 1173 LOC with tightly coupled calculation logic. The factory pattern exists but doesn't provide clear abstraction for different calculation strategies.

locations.snippet: Complex portfolio calculation logic with ROAI, TWR, MWR strategies

findings.suggested_fix: Create PortfolioCalculationStrategy interface and separate implementations for each strategy (ROAI, TWR, MWR, ROI)

findings.title: Tight coupling between portfolio service and calculator components
findings.description: The portfolio.service.ts directly instantiates and uses portfolio-calculator without dependency injection for the calculator factory, creating tight coupling and making testing difficult.

locations.snippet: Portfolio service instantiates calculator directly without abstraction

findings.suggested_fix: Inject PortfolioCalculatorFactory as dependency and define clear interface for calculator operations

findings.title: Missing abstraction for data provider implementations
findings.description: Multiple data provider services (yahoo-finance.service.ts, coingecko.service.ts, alpha-vantage.service.ts, etc.) exist but lack a consistent interface contract. Each implements different error handling and retry logic.

locations.snippet: Multiple provider implementations with inconsistent interfaces and patterns

findings.suggested_fix: Define strict DataProviderInterface and ensure all providers implement it consistently. Use Strategy pattern for provider selection.

findings.title: Configuration scattered across multiple locations
findings.description: Configuration values are found in: environment files, config.ts in libs/common, configuration.service.ts in API, and environment.ts in client. This creates inconsistency and makes configuration management difficult.

locations.snippet: Configuration constants mixed with business logic
Runtime configuration management
Environment-specific configuration

findings.suggested_fix: Centralize configuration in a single ConfigurationService with clear separation: build-time (environment files) and runtime (ConfigService)

findings.title: Missing repository/data access layer abstraction
findings.description: Services directly use Prisma client without a repository pattern. Changes to data access patterns require modifying multiple service files. No data access abstraction layer exists.

locations.snippet: Direct Prisma calls without repository abstraction

findings.suggested_fix: Create repository classes for each domain entity (PortfolioRepository, UserRepository, OrderRepository) to abstract data access

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling patterns across modules
findings.description: Error handling varies significantly: some services throw custom errors, others return null/undefined, some use try-catch blocks inconsistently. Data provider errors use specific error classes but other services don't.

locations.snippet: Custom error classes exist only for data providers

findings.suggested_fix: Define ApplicationError hierarchy and use consistently across all services. Create specific error types for each domain.

findings.title: High coupling between API routes and services
findings.description: Controllers directly instantiate and call multiple services with business logic validation occurring in controllers. Routes should delegate validation to service layer.

locations.snippet: Controller contains business logic validation and complex service orchestration

findings.suggested_fix: Move validation and orchestration logic to service layer. Controllers should only handle HTTP concerns.

findings.title: Missing clear domain boundaries between modules
findings.description: Portfolio, Order, Account, and Holding domains have unclear boundaries. Multiple services handle overlapping concerns (portfolio.service handles holdings, order.service, holdings are in portfolio calculations).

locations.snippet: Portfolio service manages holdings, orders, and accounts without clear boundaries

findings.suggested_fix: Define clear domain boundaries: Portfolio (aggregate root) -> Holdings -> Orders -> Accounts. Use explicit interfaces for inter-domain communication.

findings.title: Complex event listener dependencies without clear propagation model
findings.description: Asset and Portfolio change events have listeners (asset-profile-changed.listener.ts, portfolio-changed.listener.ts) but the event propagation model is unclear. Changes in one aggregate may trigger cascading updates without clear dependency tracking.

locations.snippet: Event listener with unclear scope of impact
Asset change listener may trigger portfolio recalculations

findings.suggested_fix: Document event propagation model explicitly. Consider using saga pattern for complex cross-aggregate transactions.

findings.title: UI library mixes component library with business logic services
findings.description: The libs/ui library (libs/ui/src/lib) contains both reusable UI components and business logic services (data.service.ts, admin.service.ts). UI library should only contain presentational components.

locations.snippet: Business logic service in UI library (883 LOC)
Admin business logic in UI library (286 LOC)

findings.suggested_fix: Move data.service.ts and admin.service.ts to apps/client or create separate business-logic library. UI library should only export components.

findings.title: Inconsistent module organization between API and client
findings.description: API uses feature-based modules (portfolio, account, order, etc.) while client uses page-based organization with nested component directories. Makes feature tracking and shared patterns unclear.

locations.snippet: Feature-based module organization
Page-based organization without clear feature boundaries

findings.suggested_fix: Align client organization with API: create feature-based modules (portfolio-feature, account-feature, etc.) containing pages, components, services.

findings.title: Missing abstraction layer for external API integrations
findings.description: Multiple external data providers (AlphaVantage, Yahoo Finance, CoinGecko) are integrated directly into services without circuit breaker, retry, or rate limiting abstractions. Makes resilience patterns scattered.

locations.snippet: Direct HTTP calls to external API without abstraction

findings.suggested_fix: Create HttpClient abstraction layer with retry, circuit breaker, rate limiting, and timeout patterns. Use decorator or strategy pattern for resilience.

findings.title: Common library mixes DTOs, utilities, types, and configurations
findings.description: libs/common contains DTOs (40+ files), types (20+ files), utilities, configurations, and interfaces all at the same level. This creates a dumping ground without clear organization.

locations.snippet: Mixed concerns: DTOs, types, utils, config, interfaces without subdomain organization

findings.suggested_fix: Reorganize libs/common by domain: /portfolio (DTOs, types, interfaces), /user, /order, etc. Move utilities to /shared/utils with subdirectories by concern.

coupling_assessment: The codebase exhibits significant coupling issues across multiple dimensions: (1) Horizontal coupling - multiple god modules (portfolio.service, admin.service, data-provider.service) create bottlenecks; (2) Vertical coupling - controllers depend on multiple service implementations without abstraction; (3) Library coupling - UI library improperly contains business logic services; (4) Data coupling - direct Prisma usage bypasses repository abstraction. The event-driven architecture adds coupling complexity without clear propagation models. Backend and frontend lack consistent architectural patterns, making changes in one area unpredictable.
layering_assessment: The codebase lacks a proper layering architecture: Missing repository/persistence abstraction layer - services directly use Prisma. Missing domain/business logic abstraction - calculations and complex logic are tightly coupled to services. Missing API gateway/service facade - controllers directly orchestrate multiple services. Missing configuration abstraction - config scattered across environment files and services. The UI library contains business logic that should be in a separate layer. While NestJS modules provide structural boundaries, the internal organization within modules doesn't follow layering principles. Data flow is unclear between layers.
summary: The codebase has 48/100 structural coherence score due to several critical architectural issues: (1) Three god modules exceeding 700+ LOC (portfolio, admin, data-provider services) violate single responsibility; (2) Missing clear abstraction layers (repository pattern, data access abstraction); (3) Inconsistent error handling patterns; (4) Configuration scattered across multiple locations; (5) Business logic mixed into UI library; (6) Unclear domain boundaries between portfolio, orders, accounts, and holdings; (7) High coupling between controllers and services; (8) Inconsistent module organization between backend (feature-based) and frontend (page-based). The event-driven architecture adds complexity without clear event propagation documentation. Immediate refactoring needed: split god modules, implement repository pattern, establish clear domain boundaries, consolidate configuration, separate UI from business logic, and create consistent abstraction layers across API and client.
